standard_prerequisites.name: Finite generation of the graded module of cohomology along powers of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F (invoked at proof line 4287)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies finitely many elements $x_i \in H^p(X, I^{d_i}\mathcal{F})$ generating $\bigoplus_{n \geq 0} H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ over $B = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} I^n$, which is what produces the constant $c = \max\{d_i\}$.

standard_prerequisites.name: The situation of formal functions: the algebraic space, the ideal sheaf and the module
standard_prerequisites.use: It fixes the ambient data $X$, $I$ and $\mathcal{F}$ in which both conclusions are formulated, including the graded ring $B$ acting on the graded module.

core_obligations: Apply the finite generation statement to obtain degrees $d_1, \ldots, d_t$ and elements $x_i \in H^p(X, I^{d_i}\mathcal{F})$ generating the graded module over $B$, and set $c = \max\{d_i\}$ (proof lines 4287-4291).
Read off part (1): generation over $B$ says exactly that the multiplication map $I^{n-c} \otimes H^p(X, I^c\mathcal{F}) \to H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ is surjective for $n \geq c$ (proof line 4292).

For part (2), set $b = \max(0, n-c)$ and write down the commutative diagram relating $I^{n+m-c-b} \otimes I^b \otimes H^p(X, I^c\mathcal{F})$ and $I^{n+m-c-b} \otimes H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ to $H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ (proof lines 4293-4304).

Conclude: the composition is surjective by part (1) when $n + m \geq c$, and $n + m - c - b \geq m - c$, so the image of $H^p(X, I^{n+m}\mathcal{F}) \to H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ lies in $I^{m-c}H^p(X, I^n\mathcal{F})$ (proof lines 4305-4307).
proof_roadmap: Generators of the graded module and the constant $c$ (proof lines 4287-4291).
The commutative diagram for part (2) (proof lines 4293-4304).
Surjectivity of the composition and the containment (proof lines 4305-4307).
difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the grading of the cohomology along powers of the ideal effective: a single constant $c$ bounds both the generation of each graded piece from $I^c\mathcal{F}$ and the gain in the ideal that the transition maps produce (statement lines 4272-4284). The proof extracts the constant from a finite generating set of the graded module, reads part (1) off directly, and then verifies part (2) through a commutative diagram whose horizontal composition is surjective by part (1). The bookkeeping of the two exponents is the substance, so the claim is H2.
